0xPhilipp – (deleted reply, maybe glitch)“We would prefer personal responses rather than walls of AI-generated text, but your points are pretty simple.

  1. Three Emergency Supervisors is fine with me and most likely the others too, as long as they meet the requirements and there is broad agreement within PF (and the community). We already reached that for the two names mentioned.
  2. An open application process can be done through this forum thread. Anyone who wants to be considered can put themselves forward, show that they meet the stated requirements, disclose any relevant relationships, and explain why they are suitable. The community can then comment openly before the final candidates are selected. I’ll also coordinate with PF so our view on whether someone meets the criteria is given here transparently. If no suitable third person can be found, the proposal will still go ahead with only 1, so it should not block the process. Target for on-chain publishing is end of next week.
  3. I agree that PF’s structure should be improved, but that should not be mixed into this process in a way that prevents accountability from happening. The current issue needs to be resolved first. After that, I expect we will propose a broader Stewardship structure. David suggested a model roughly inspired by the UN Security Council, with three core seats and two 12-months rotating seats, which I think could work well and bringing in new fresh blood. We have already reached out to potential candidates that would be a good fit, but they will only be able to take part in real talks after the house has been cleaned.

Yes, this process can have a major impact on the ecosystem. That is exactly why it is necessary. PF needs to get back into a position where it can actually act, especially with more security incidents, infrastructure problems and fires to put out.

We need a Foundation that is pulling in the same direction and focused on protecting and growing Terra, not one consumed by internal political fights, downplaying security issues, lethargy and non-contribution or slowly turning Terra into Terra Classic through stagnation, risk aversion and an inability to act.”

Reply:

As you know, English is not my first language, so yes, I use AI to help correct my grammar and express my thoughts more clearly. But I don’t think that should be the point of discussion; what matters is the substance of the arguments.

I appreciate that you agree the Foundation needs improvement and that having three Emergency Supervisors is a reasonable approach. I also agree that the current situation needs to be addressed without unnecessary delays.

Regarding the selection of candidates, I believe this should ultimately be decided through community governance. The application process should be open, transparent and give the community a genuine opportunity to assess the candidates, rather than leaving the decision mainly to the Foundation itself.

On the question of improving the Foundation’s structure, my point was not to delay accountability. Quite the opposite. I believe we could use this opportunity to address the immediate problem while also laying the groundwork for a stronger and more decentralised structure in the future.

If we are already appointing independent people to help resolve the current situation, why not take the opportunity to consider how we can bring more experience, different perspectives and new contributors into the Foundation? This could help us address not only the immediate dispute but also some of the structural weaknesses that may have contributed to it.

Of course, the emergency process should have a clear mandate and should not be held up by broader reforms. But resolving the current issue and improving the Foundation do not have to be mutually exclusive.

My concern remains that we should not place so much responsibility in the hands of one person, or predetermine the outcome before the process has run its course. We should give the community a meaningful role in selecting the people involved and ensure that the process is fair, transparent and independent.

Ultimately, we all want a stronger Foundation that can protect and develop Terra. I believe we have an opportunity here not only to resolve the current situation, but also to take a positive step towards making the Foundation more accountable, decentralised and representative of the community.
